credit: Written for the app from the New York, 1925 city data and the history of that year.

factions.name: Tammany Hall
factions.about: The Democratic machine on 14th Street: jobs, coal and favors for votes.

factions.name: The Citizens Union
factions.about: Good-government reformers who want the machine out of City Hall.

factions.name: The Anti-Saloon League
factions.about: The drys, who won Prohibition and mean to see it enforced.

factions.name: The bootleggers
factions.about: The rum-runners and speakeasy owners who keep the city wet and the police paid.

factions.name: The garment unions
factions.about: Cutters, cloakmakers and dressmakers of the Lower East Side, organized and quarrelling among themselves.

factions.name: The Chamber of Commerce
factions.about: Bankers and merchants of the Financial District.

factions.name: The police
factions.about: The city's police, some of them on the take.

questions.title: Walker or Hylan
questions.question: Should Jimmy Walker take the mayor's chair from Hylan?

sides.name: Walker
sides.stand: see Jimmy Walker in City Hall

beats: Hylan promised to keep the five-cent fare.
Walker was seen at a Broadway opening past three in the morning.

questions.title: The five-cent fare
questions.question: Should the subway fare stay at a nickel?

sides.name: Raise it
sides.stand: let the companies raise the fare

sides.name: Keep the nickel
sides.stand: keep the fare at five cents

beats: The subway companies say they are losing money.
Straphangers packed a hearing at City Hall.
